figs.cap: : Composite bilayer kagome results at N=768/layer. (a) Monopole density ρₘ vs. quantum-drive proxy Γ_eff for all J_⊥/J₁ values; error bars are binomial standard errors. (b) Effective chemical-potential proxy μₘon^eff/J₁ [Eq. ( 4 )]; classical reference 2J₁ (dotted) and deconfinement threshold μ_c=0.808 J₁ (dashed red) are indicated. The persistent gap above μ_c is a quantitative measure of the hardware distance from deconfinement. (c) Monopole pair correlation G(r) at three representative annealing times (J_⊥/J₁=0.5); exponential decay confirms the confined phase at all conditions. (d) All-plaquette charge structure factor S_Q(k^*) vs. system size N at tₐ=5 ns; the absence of N-dependence contrasts with the strong ice-manifold signal in Fig. 5 and is explained by defect dilution. (e) I

: Transition characterisation from the dedicated Cₛ^⊥ analysis. (a) Slow-anneal order-parameter curves for all four system sizes, showing the direct sign reversal near (J_⊥/J₁)^*≈ 0.044. (b) Slow-anneal Binder cumulants crossing in the same window; the dashed line at U₄=2/3 marks the ordered-phase limit. (c) Zero-crossing phase boundary stable within 0.042–0.046 over 10 ns≤ tₐ≤ 500 μs; the upward shift only at the non-adiabatic 5 ns point confirms that the transition coupling is a ground-state property of the bilayer exchange. (d) Phase diagram in (log₁₀Γ_eff, J_⊥/J₁) space at N=768, with the critical line marking the ferroelectric-to-antiferroelectric boundary.
